title: Instant Analytics Dashboard Factory
description: Pick a curated sample dataset, watch Claude profile it via streaming animation, get a fully designed interactive dashboard. Two modes: ad-hoc analysis for business users, hi-fi wireframes for BI engineers.

resumeBullet.text: Architected an AI-powered dashboard factory on Next.js + Vercel — unified design-token system across 6 business domains, streaming AI profiling with hand-curated fixtures, automatic KPI / chart recommendation, and dataset-driven hi-fi wireframes designed for Figma MCP handoff. Reduces ad-hoc dashboard turnaround from days to minutes.

portfolioCard.problem: Dashboard creation is slow and unstructured. A VP wants Q3 vs Q2 regional sales by Monday; the typical path is a BI ticket plus a three-day wait for something that looks like Excel circa 2012. Meanwhile BI engineers spend 2-4 days mocking dashboards in Figma before the real build, for stakeholder discovery and alignment. Two audiences, two timelines, one underlying cause.
portfolioCard.approach: Two modes, one shared chart engine. Ad-hoc mode (business users): pick a CSV, watch Claude profile it via streaming explanation, get an interactive dashboard with filters, drill-downs, and PDF export in about a minute. Wireframe mode (BI engineers and designers): pick a dataset-driven wireframe, each layout generated from the dataset schema by the same engine that powers the ad-hoc dashboard, ready to share in a stakeholder discovery session or hand off via the future-state Figma MCP integration.
portfolioCard.impact: Ad-hoc dashboard turnaround drops from days to minutes. BI engineers save 3-4 days of pre-discovery Figma rebuilds per project. The unified design system means every output looks like it came from a professional BI team, regardless of which mode produced it. See the case study for architecture, key decisions, and the W5.D4.x engineering-moments narrative.
